title: Free-variable count of the Razborov encoding's output
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ Boolean variables in which no term repeats a literal, and within each term any two literals on the same variable coincide (so each variable occurs at most once per term). Let $\rho$ be a restriction with exactly $s$ free variables, and let $w$ and $d$ be natural numbers with $d \le s$. Suppose $\rho$ is bad for $f$ at depth $d$, meaning the restricted Boolean function $f|_\rho$ has decision-tree depth strictly greater than $d$. Then the restriction forming the first component of the Razborov encoding of $f$ and $\rho$ with parameters $w$ and $d$ has exactly $s - d$ free variables.
hypotheses_covered: ρ has exactly s free variables
ρ is bad for f at depth d (decision-tree depth of f|_ρ exceeds d)
within each term, two literals on the same variable coincide
each term has no repeated literal
replaced:
For a bad $s$-restriction $\rho$ with $d \leq s$, the first component
(the $\gamma$-output) of $\mathrm{razborovEncode}\,f\,w\,d\,\rho$ is an
$(s-d)$-restriction, since the encoder fixes exactly $d$ previously free
variables.
